purpose.text: Support requested GA4 website traffic, content, audience, engagement, conversion and revenue analysis; Search Console search-performance analysis; and URL indexing, removal or inspection, with saved results and human-readable analysis summaries. These are alternative supported operations, not evidence of authorization to perform them.

evidences.reason: Defines the toolkit's analytical and indexing purposes and request-driven applicability.
Defines the analysis, persistence and summary workflow.
Adds URL removal and inspection as supported operations.

requirements.text: For operational setup, install the script dependencies before using the toolkit.

evidences.reason: Explicitly instructs dependency installation in the scripts directory.

requirements.text: Configure the GA4 property identifier, service-account email and private key, Search Console site URL, and default date range through a project-root .env file. Operational prerequisites are a Google Cloud project with the Analytics Data, Search Console and Indexing APIs enabled and a service account with access to the GA4 property and Search Console. The displayed example values do not identify an actual authorized property, account or site.

evidences.reason: Specifies configuration fields, configuration location and access prerequisites using example values.

requirements.text: For each analysis, follow the stated order: call the applicable Google APIs to obtain structured data, save the results, then read the saved JSON files to prepare the summary.

evidences.reason: Explicitly establishes three ordered phases for every analysis.

requirements.text: When a custom GA4 report is requested, use its required dimensions and metrics and its applicable date range, dimension filters, sort order and row limit.

evidences.reason: Defines the custom-report inputs and their roles, including optional filtering, ordering and limiting.

requirements.text: Automatically save analysis results as timestamped JSON under the applicable results category. Preserve the result data in a metadata wrapper rather than replacing it with a summary. Explicit save controls on individual API calls permit opting out of those individual saves; high-level orchestration still saves its final result.

evidences.reason: States the general automatic persistence duty.
Requires saving the supplied result data with a metadata wrapper.
Documents an explicit save control with saving enabled by default.
Demonstrates individual saves being disabled while the final comparison is saved.

requirements.text: Name saved JSON files using a YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS timestamp followed by the operation name and, when supplied, extra information separated by double underscores. Store standard GA4 reports, realtime results, Search Console results and indexing results in their respective results subdirectories.

evidences.reason: Specifies the filename pattern and category-based storage.
Identifies the result categories and their directory names.
Distinguishes required category and operation information from optional filename information.

requirements.text: After analysis, create a Markdown summary in results/summaries/ using the saved JSON files, including data tables, trends and recommendations.

evidences.reason: Explicitly requires the summary location, source data and content.

requirements.text: For operations that take a date range, support day-count shorthand and explicit start and end dates. GA4 report ranges also support GA4 relative-date objects; Search Console ranges require calendar dates. Use the configured default date range when omitted, with 30d as the fallback.

evidences.reason: Defines date formats and the configurable default.
Specifies Search Console's calendar-date requirement and shorthand conversion.
Specifies configured defaults, object ranges and shorthand conversion for GA4 reports.

requirements.text: When a comprehensive site overview is requested, include page-view, traffic-source, demographic and event results for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Defines the site-overview composition.
Preserves the same date-range relationship across the four component reports.

requirements.text: When traffic analysis is requested, include source data, sessions by source and medium, and new-versus-returning user results. The source/medium session report includes sessions, engagedSessions, averageSessionDuration and bounceRate; the newVsReturning report includes activeUsers, sessions and conversions.

evidences.reason: Defines the three traffic-analysis components.
Specifies the dimensions and metrics of the component session and returning-user reports.

requirements.text: When content performance is requested, include page views, landing-page results and exit-page results for the applicable date range. Landing-page results use landingPage with sessions, activeUsers, bounceRate and averageSessionDuration; exit-page results use pagePath with exits and screenPageViews.

evidences.reason: Defines the required content-analysis components.
Specifies the landing-page and exit-page report information.

requirements.text: When user-behavior analysis is requested, include demographics, events and daily engagement results for the applicable date range. Daily engagement uses date with activeUsers, engagedSessions, engagementRate and averageSessionDuration.

evidences.reason: Defines the demographic, event and daily-engagement components.
Specifies the daily engagement information and shared date range.

requirements.text: When comparing periods, obtain results for both supplied date ranges using the same selected dimensions and metrics, and preserve each period's date range alongside its corresponding data. The default comparison dimensions are date and the default metrics are activeUsers, sessions and screenPageViews.

evidences.reason: Defines the two-period comparison purpose.
Specifies comparison defaults and the association between each range and its report.

requirements.text: When a live snapshot is requested, include current active users, current pages and current events. Active users and page views are grouped by unifiedScreenName; event counts are grouped by eventName.

evidences.reason: Defines the three live-snapshot components.
Defines the grouping and returned information for the component realtime operations.

requirements.text: When page-view data is requested, report pagePath and pageTitle with screenPageViews, activeUsers and averageSessionDuration for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Specifies the page-view report's dimensions and metrics.

requirements.text: When traffic-source data is requested, report sessionSource, sessionMedium and sessionCampaignName with sessions, activeUsers, newUsers and bounceRate for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Specifies the source report's dimensions and metrics.

requirements.text: When demographic data is requested, report country, deviceCategory and browser with activeUsers, sessions and newUsers for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Defines demographics as country, device and browser breakdowns with the listed metrics.

requirements.text: When event-count data is requested, report eventName with eventCount, eventCountPerUser and activeUsers for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Specifies the event-count report information.

requirements.text: When conversion data is requested, report eventName and sessionSource with conversions and totalRevenue for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Specifies conversion grouping and metrics.

requirements.text: When ecommerce revenue data is requested, report date and transactionId with totalRevenue, ecommercePurchases and averagePurchaseRevenue for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Explicitly includes transaction-level identity in the revenue report.

requirements.text: When realtime traffic-source data is requested, report active users by firstUserSource and firstUserMedium.

evidences.reason: Specifies the realtime source breakdown.

requirements.text: When a Search Console overview is requested, include top queries, top pages, device performance and country performance for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Defines the SEO overview composition.
Associates all four component reports with the same requested range.

requirements.text: When keyword analysis is requested, provide search-query results and a device breakdown for the applicable date range. Whether the device breakdown must be associated with each query or may be a separate aggregate report remains unresolved.

evidences.reason: Describes queries with a device breakdown.
Provides separate query and device reports rather than a query-by-device report.

requirements.text: When SEO page-performance analysis is requested, provide top-page results and a country breakdown for the applicable date range. The top-page ranking criterion remains unresolved between clicks and impressions.

evidences.reason: Specifies top pages by clicks and a country breakdown.
Uses the shared top-page function and a separate country report.
Describes the shared top-page function as ranking by impressions.

requirements.text: When a custom Search Console analytics query is requested, use its dimensions, date range, row limit and pagination offset. Defaults are query as the dimension, 1000 rows and offset 0. Supported documented dimensions are query, page, device, country and searchAppearance; returned rows contain keys, clicks, impressions, ctr and position.

evidences.reason: Defines query controls, defaults and returned row information.

requirements.text: When top search queries are requested, return the top 100 queries by clicks for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Specifies the ranking metric and maximum result count.

requirements.text: When the top-page Search Console operation is requested, return up to 100 pages for the applicable date range. Preserve the unresolved source distinction between ranking by impressions and ranking by clicks; do not require both rankings.

evidences.reason: Specifies 100 pages ranked by impressions.
Describes the same top-page function as ranking by clicks.

requirements.text: When Search Console device performance is requested, provide a breakdown by device type, including desktop, mobile and tablet.

evidences.reason: Defines the requested device breakdown.

requirements.text: When Search Console country performance is requested, provide search-performance results for the top 50 countries for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Specifies country grouping and the top-50 limit.

requirements.text: When search-appearance data is requested, provide Search Console performance by searchAppearance for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Defines the search-appearance operation.
Specifies searchAppearance as the grouping dimension.

requirements.text: When indexing is requested for a specified full URL, submit a recrawl notification for that URL and return its URL_UPDATED notification result with the URL and notification time.

evidences.reason: Defines the target URL, indexing side effect and notification result.

requirements.text: When indexing multiple URLs, process the supplied URLs sequentially to avoid rate limiting and return results for the batch. For the high-level reindexing operation, retain each URL's submitted or failed status and its error when it fails.

evidences.reason: Explicitly requires sequential batch processing.
Preserves each URL's individual submission outcome while continuing through the batch.

requirements.text: When removal of a specified URL from Google's index is requested, submit the removal notification for that URL and return a URL_DELETED result with the URL and notification time. This is a separate operation from recrawling or inspection.

evidences.reason: Defines the removal side effect and its distinct notification type.

requirements.text: When inspecting a specified URL, provide its index status, coverage state, last-crawl information, mobile usability and rich-result information as available from the inspection result.

evidences.reason: Defines the inspection purpose and returned status information.
Distinguishes required index-status structure from optional crawl, mobile and rich-result information.

requirements.text: When checking index status for multiple URLs through the high-level operation, retain each URL with its index-status result and an indexed flag that is true when the inspection verdict is PASS. If inspection fails, retain the URL, an indexed value of false and the error in its status result.

evidences.reason: Defines URL-to-status association, the indexed condition and failure representation.

requirements.text: When available GA4 fields are requested, provide the property's available dimensions and metrics. Dimension-only and metric-only operations return their respective metadata, including apiName, uiName and description; the full-property metadata operation returns the full metadata response.

evidences.reason: Defines the available-fields operation.
Distinguishes dimension-only, metric-only and full metadata results.

requirements.text: For bulk page-path lookup, trim whitespace and add a leading slash when missing while preserving trailing slashes.

evidences.reason: Explicitly defines normalization and the trailing-slash preservation duty.

requirements.text: For a nonempty bulk page-path lookup, restrict the report to the normalized supplied page paths using case-insensitive pagePath membership. An empty path list produces an empty report with rowCount 0 without issuing a report request.

evidences.reason: Defines the page-path filter and its case-insensitive membership semantics.
Associates the normalized paths with the request and explicitly handles an empty list before the API call.

requirements.text: For bulk page-path lookup, return the selected metrics for each requested path with pagePath and pageTitle. Unless custom metrics are supplied, retrieve screenPageViews, activeUsers, averageSessionDuration, bounceRate and engagementRate for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Defines path-specific metrics, custom metric selection and defaults.
Specifies the path and title dimensions of the bulk report.

requirements.text: When listing saved results, restrict the listing to the specified category, sort newest first and apply the supplied maximum count when present.

evidences.reason: Defines category scope, ordering and the optional result limit.

requirements.text: When loading a saved result, use the specified JSON filepath and return its saved-result wrapper, or null when the result cannot be loaded.

evidences.reason: Defines filepath-specific loading and its nullable saved-result return.

requirements.text: When retrieving the latest saved result, select the most recent result in the specified category, restricted to the specified operation when one is supplied, and return a saved result or null.

evidences.reason: Defines recency selection, category scope and optional operation filtering.
Lists multiple request-dependent analytical and indexing purposes.
Maps distinct user requests to distinct operations rather than selecting one operation.
Includes removal and inspection as additional distinct branches.

issues.reason: The frozen source defines a toolkit with alternative purposes but does not select an actual operational request or establish authorization. Retain the branches conditionally; do not combine them into a requirement to collect all supported data or perform every indexing action.

evidences.reason: States that every analysis follows automatic saving before summarization.
Permits controlling whether an individual report is saved.
Disables individual comparison-report saves while saving the combined comparison.

issues.reason: Apply the explicit save option as a specific exception for individual API calls. Preserve automatic saving of high-level final analysis results and the saved-data summary workflow. Do not interpret automatic saving as requiring a separate file for every intermediate call.

evidences.reason: Broadly states that all functions accept the listed date formats, including GA4 relative dates.
Explicitly distinguishes Search Console calendar dates from GA4 relative dates.
Lists realtime, URL and metadata functions whose documented signatures do not take date ranges.

issues.reason: Limit date-range requirements to date-taking operations and follow the explicit service-specific date distinction. Retain shorthand and explicit calendar dates for Search Console and GA4 relative-date objects for GA4 reports; do not require date arguments for realtime, indexing or metadata operations.

evidences.reason: Defines SEO page performance using top pages by clicks.
Defines the shared top-page function using search impressions.
Calls the shared top-page function while describing the result as pages by clicks.
Also describes the standalone top-page function as pages by clicks.

issues.reason: Clicks and impressions are competing ranking criteria for the same operation. The supplied sources do not establish which criterion controls. Preserve the top-page result and count obligations while leaving ranking unresolved; requiring both rankings would broaden the task.

evidences.reason: Describes keyword analysis as queries with a device breakdown.
Returns a query report and a separate device-performance report.
The device-performance report groups only by device.

issues.reason: The descriptive contract can mean a device breakdown for each query, whereas the implementation supplies an independent aggregate device breakdown. These interpretations require different associations and information. Preserve query results and device information without silently requiring both representations or declaring the aggregate interpretation sufficient.
